findings.issue: prepare()'s catch-all maps every bootstrap failure (config drift deny, identity mismatch throw, unsupported model) to reason 'resources_unavailable', which misdirects user diagnostics even though the explicit-mismatch branch inside the try correctly uses 'config_changed'. Behavior is fail-closed; only the reported reason is wrong.
findings.minimalFix: In the catch, inspect the error (e.g. AssistantAnalysisProviderUnavailableError vs resource errors) and set reason='config_changed' for identity/configuration failures, keeping 'resources_unavailable' only for resource-layer failures.

findings.issue: current()'s single catch conflates store read failures and readCurrentModel() transport errors with genuine identity drift, always reporting 'config_changed'. Safe direction (provider is cleared, never resurrected), but the reason can mislead.
findings.minimalFix: Catch readCurrentModel()/comparison failures separately from store errors, or add a distinct reason value for store/runtime errors.

findings.issue: A process crash between the atomic link() (line 86) and unlink() (line 87) leaves an orphaned '.manifest-<uuid>.tmp' inside the leaf. Cruft is harmless (verify/manifest comparison ignore leaf-root extras; link() still refuses to replace an existing manifest), but stale temps are never swept.
findings.minimalFix: On prepare, best-effort remove leaf entries matching /^\.manifest-.*\.tmp$/ owned by this uid before or after publishManifest.

resolved: Prior P1-1 (provider identity drift / silent replacement) is repaired and type-correct: settings.prepare() (line 27) compares provider.modelId to the requested modelId, re-reads the durable selection and requires selection.modelId===modelId and selection.revision===revision captured before bootstrap, and requires JSON.stringify(provider.readCurrentModel())===JSON.stringify(provider.identity); settings.current() (line 17) compares selected modelId, providerRevision, and live identity against the pinned identity and on any mismatch or throw clears this.provider AND providerRevision with reason 'config_changed' — no implicit resurrection (test line 14 confirms drifted provider stays cleared after drift subsides). The prior reviewer's suggested readCurrentModel()!==modelId comparison is correctly NOT used, since readCurrentModel returns {modelEpoch,configFingerprint}.

Bootstrap returns the local configuration modelId (provider.ts line 94 returns input modelId; contract.model carries the wire model), verified by counter-test lines 73-80 expecting modelId 'p3-explicit-selection' with contract.model 'deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp'.

Prior P2-2 resolved: restore() now guards `if(this.preparing)return this.status()` (settings line 21), and configure() throws when preparing (line 24) with preparing set synchronously before any await, so same-process configure/restore races are excluded; cross-prepare revision changes are detected via the re-read selection.revision.

Prior P2-3 crash window redesigned per spec: manifest is never generated in stage (avoids stale absolute paths); after rename the fresh leaf is fully re-verified (asset hashes, inspectDeepSeekRecipeEnvironment, freeze, calibration===7) before publishManifest writes+fsyncs a private 0600 random temp and hard-links atomically, never replacing an existing target (link() fails EEXIST), then unlinks its own temp; only ENOENT manifest permits recovery via explicit prepare; existing invalid/directory/symlink manifests go through strict regularFile+content comparison and are never overwritten (counter-tests lines 47-72); restoreAssistantAnalysisResources is validation-only (paths(create=false), no network/writes).

Authorization path unchanged and conformant: streamStatelessSideCallProviderConversation with existing adapter/SDK, maxRetries 0 at both client and call level, full-body binding via overridden create (byte-identical serializedBody else abort+throw), native chunks buffered before adapter normalization with raw finish (stop/length only) and raw final usage (safe-integer validated, 'unknown' otherwise — no estimates), single attemptId consumption, owner AbortController with signal forwarding and timeout mapping to 'timeout'/'cancelled', and ContractBreach carrying actual usage on both success and error paths; no raw SDK bypass observed.

Model allowlist enforced: only deepseek first_party/openai_legacy with baseUrl https://api.deepseek.com[/v1] and wire model in the pinned WIRE_MODELS alias list; empty model string, unknown providers, forged counters and qwen-style models are rejected with no implicit fallback (tests lines 109-118); capacity counting uses the official pinned deepseek-flash frozen recipe/tokenizer only, no chars/4.

Resource supply-chain checks confirmed in-source: dual pinned sha256 assets, redirect:'error', 64MB streaming cap, 'wx' 0600 writes, EXTRACT whitelist of 7 pinned members with absolute/dot-dot/backslash/symlink/encryption/size validation, spawn without shell under -I -S -B with minimized env and output/timeout caps, lstat-based symlink and mode-022 rejection, uid ownership on directories, mkdtemp staging with rename install and rm cleanup, pending-map dedupe per dataRoot+python key.

Error status handling: AssistantAnalysisProviderFailure propagates the actual integer HTTP status (400-599) from the SDK error with no speculative quota attribution, and no retry loop exists for 402/429/500 (tests lines 41-46 verify single fetch).
limitations: Static review only of the frozen bundle (SHA256 387564c7e5fb66c4ee730c55cc5ef67c303b9200014f67190d83aaefc29a6493). I did not execute any tests, builds, or live calls; the cited '31 tests passed' and the in-flight settings-test/build reruns are reported by others and are not verified by me; this review is not end-to-end activation, pilot, or package qualification.

Not in the frozen bundle and therefore reviewed by interface only: OpenAIAdapter.stream internals (signal wiring to the underlying fetch/SDK, relied upon for timeout/cancel), createAdapterFromBinding, resolveRuntimeModelBinding, LoopStore.transaction semantics, transport-lease, model-harness-identity, and main.ts beyond the excerpt.

Optimistic-revision selection is airtight within the single Electron main process (preparing guard + same-connection transaction); cross-process concurrent configure against the same SQLite file would rely on single-main-process ownership, which is architectural but not proven in this bundle.
Hardcoded wheel/tokenizer/package-member sha256 values were not re-verified against upstream artifacts (no network access in this review).

Known limitation classified honestly per task: root model identity is config-bytes hash + mtime; live binding drift within a process is caught (readCurrentModel re-resolves and compares the full pinned binding), but cross-restart environment-only credential changes may not alter the persisted raw-config identity — a restarted bootstrap re-pins whatever the environment then resolves. Root helper/grant identity belongs to the main owner and is broader pending work, not assessed as an in-scope defect here.

Explicit host trust: local Python/runtime hash snapshot trusts the host at provision time; a same-UID malicious arbitrary-code host is outside the isolation claim, so residual lstat/rename TOCTOU against same-UID attackers is accepted by design.
